name: Mirador's Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
tags_json: {"colour:back": "red", "colour:text": "white", "information": "board", "inscription": "Named after Kyoto's top sight and selfie walk, near the Tenryu-ji Temple, Mirador's path through its heritage and eco park passes through rows of tall bamboo of the species Phyllostachys edulis \"Heterocycla,\"", "inscription:1": "that grows every now and then \"tortoise shell bamboo.\"", "inscription:10": "Suitable canes are then cleaned, scraped, carved and ornamented while still fresh, then sun-dried for a week or more until the canes harden as moisture evaporates.", "inscription:11": "These are then oil-stained and finished by MJV staff.", "inscription:12": "The tortoise shell staff are available for those who wish to use one while walking the trail of Mirador Heritage and Eco Park and to bring back as a souvenir of a place,", "inscription:13": "highlighted by the Department of Tourism as on of a number of \"Beautiful Destinations\" in Baguio.", "inscription:14": "Walk safely with the help of a rarity from nature and creative human hands.", "inscription:2": "It is called \"tortoise\" because the lower part of the bamboo from the root to about 60 cm. can display the habit of shortened internodes alternately facing each other so that the internodes resemble a tortoise shell.", "inscription:3": "It is called \"Kikko\" in Japanese meaning \"tortoise\" and it related to the edible Moso bamboo.", "inscription:4": "The Kikko is not a seperate species of Phyllostachys, one of three commonly planted genus of \"running\" or monopodial bamboo. The other two are Hibanobambusa and Qiongzhuea. Unlike the tropical sympodial bamboo", "inscription:5": "where a mother plant shoots out underground stems called rhizomes in a radial pattern, from which new plants grow, the monopodial type shoots out rhizomes in a straight line from either side of a plant.", "inscription:6": "Hence, the running or monopodial bamboo produces a pleasing tall hedge of bamboo.", "inscription:7": "The Kikko is a genetic mutation of the Phyllostachys and the tortoise shell internode is not found in all the bamboo canes. It grows roughly about one in every 300 to 500 canes.", "inscription:8": "The bamboo with this genetic mutation is highly ornamental and quite rare.", "inscription:9": "Mirador Jesuit Villa's (MJV) gardeners sustainably harvest tortoise shell as part of its on-going maintenance of the bamboo grove to prevent it from becoming overgrown and unhealthy.", "name": "Mirador's Arashiyama Bamboo Grove", "tourism": "information"}
